title: Knowledge Snapshot Anchoring: Eval Manifest for Time-Sensitive Benchmarks
author: Priya Menon
body:
Overview:

This document specifies Redwood's recommended pattern for capturing, anchoring, and evaluating knowledge-sensitive model behavior over time. The goal is to make evals reproducible when knowledge in the world (facts, events, software versions, policy text) changes, and to provide a pragmatic operational workflow for detecting, triaging, and rolling back regressions tied to temporal drift.

Intended audience:
- Applied ML engineers running eval suites
- SREs and platform engineers managing eval-runner capacity and snapshot-store
- Product managers owning user-facing factual features

Why snapshot anchoring matters:
- LLMs are evaluated against prompts whose correct answer can change (e.g., "Who is the CEO of X?"). Without anchoring to a knowledge snapshot, test failures can look like model regressions when they are actually time drift.
- Snapshotting enables deterministic replay during regression hunts, auditability for compliance, and safer promotion of quantized / cache-optimized model variants.

Key concepts and components:
- Knowledge Snapshot: a timestamped collection of canonical references (URLs, corpus digest, curated facts) representing the world state used to generate / label probe answers.
- Probe: a single input-output test case; in time-sensitive probes the expected answer is tagged with the snapshot id and confidence window.
- Snapshot Store: service name "snapshot-store" (S3 + index in metadata DB), retention policy defined below.
- Eval Runner: service name "eval-runner" which accepts --snapshot-id for anchored runs.

Snapshot metadata schema (human-readable table):
| field | type | description | example |
|---|---|---:|---|
| snapshot_id | string | unique id (ISO date + short hash) | 2026-01-12-3f9b |
| created_at | date | creation timestamp (UTC) | 2026-01-12T09:10:00Z |
| source_manifest | string | URI to a manifest (list of source URIs + digests) | s3://snapshots/2026-01-12/manifest.json |
| curator | string | person/team curating the snapshot | data-ops / priya.menon@redwood.com |
| scope_tags | list | topical tags used for selection | politics, api-changes, finance |
| verifier_hash | string | digest of canonical labels used by probes | sha256:ab12... |

Recommended snapshot cadence and retention:
- Fast-moving domains (news, product releases): daily snapshot + 30 day retention
- Moderate cadence domains (APIs, SDKs): weekly snapshot + 90 day retention
- Stable domains (encyclopedic facts): monthly snapshot + 365 day retention
- Retention and lifecycle are configurable per tag via snapshot-store policy; default TTLs above enforced by snapshot-store garbage collector.

Probe authoring guidelines for time anchors:
1. Every probe that depends on mutable facts must include: subject, predicate, temporal-range (earliest / latest acceptable answer date), and authoritative-source URI(s).
2. For open-ended answers prefer "canonicalized response" assertions (short string or structured JSON) to free text scoring.
3. Assign an expected answer confidence level (high/medium/low) to help triage noisy labels.
4. Group probes into anchored bundles that reference the snapshot_id used to label them.

Example anchored probe (text block):
- id: probe-2026-0012
- snapshot_id: 2026-01-12-3f9b
- prompt: "Who is the current CTO of Umbra Systems?"
- expected_answer: "Rina Alvarez"
- temporal_range: "2026-01-01 to 2026-01-31"
- sources: [https://umbra.example/careers/leadership]
- confidence: high

Eval-runner integration (CLI examples):
- Run a standard anchored eval: 
  eval-runner --suite=knowledge-anchor-suite --snapshot-id=2026-01-12-3f9b --parallel=16 --output=s3://eval-results/2026-02-01/anchor-run.json
- Convert an unanchored suite into an anchored one: 
  probe-tool attach-snapshot --suite=ask-api-suite --snapshot-id=2026-01-12-3f9b --author="Priya Menon"

Anchored run SLOs and alerting thresholds:
- Regression alert if anchored accuracy delta >= 3% for high-confidence probes in a service slice over a 24-hr rolling window.
- Informational notice for 1-3% delta; requires review by probe steward.
- Latency SLO for eval-runner using snapshots: median runtime increase vs unanchored baseline <= 5%; if > 15% investigate snapshot-store hot-paths and caching.

Automated triage playbook when temporal drift is detected (numbered steps):
1. Verify the failing probes are anchored (check snapshot_id in result manifest). If not anchored, mark as unanchored candidate and queue for manual labeling.
2. Query snapshot-store to retrieve source_manifest and verifier_hash. Validate that the probe expected answer digests match the manifest.
3. Run a cross-snapshot diff: replay the probe across the latest 5 snapshots via eval-runner --snapshot-range to determine if change is persistent or transient.
4. If change is persistent across snapshots: escalate to product owner and data-ops for canon update. Create a regression issue with tag "temporal:canonical-update".
5. If change is present only in the latest snapshot: suspect snapshot-label drift. Run label verification workflow (human-in-the-loop) using the annotator CLI: annotator-verify --snapshot-id=... --probes=...
6. If model regression confirmed (answers disagree with authoritative sources for snapshot period): open a model-regression incident in incident tracker and follow the standard regression rollback playbook (link in related_pages).

Canary & rollout recommendations for snapshot-dependent model changes:
- Always run a pre-promotion anchored eval: the candidate model must pass high-confidence anchored probe set at >= baseline accuracy.
- Deploy canary to shadow traffic with anchored monitoring enabled for 48 hours for fast-moving domains, 7 days for stable domains.
- If anchored delta > threshold during canary, automatically soft-fail promotion and create a rollback task.

Governance and responsibilities:
- Snapshot curator: Data-Ops (owns snapshot cadence, manifests, and storage paths).
- Probe steward: Applied ML (owns probe quality and expected answers).
- Eval owner: Eval Platform (owns eval-runner, metrics export, and alerting integration).

Storage & naming conventions (must be followed):
- Snapshot manifest path: s3://redwood-snapshots/{domain}/{YYYY-MM-DD}/{snapshot_id}/manifest.json
- Anchored probe bundles: s3://eval-probes/anchored/{domain}/{snapshot_id}/bundle.ndjson
- Eval results: s3://eval-results/{YYYY-MM-DD}/{suite}/{snapshot_id}/results.jsonl

Example change-log / audit snippet to include in regression tickets:
- fields: [snapshot_id, probe_ids, cohort_tag, baseline_accuracy, new_accuracy, run_id, evaluator_commit, model_hash]
- policy: tickets generated by automated triage must attach the snapshot manifest and a link to the verifier hash.

Appendix A — Quick checks and heuristics for common failure modes:
- If many probes in the same domain fail and sources in manifest changed recently, treat as knowledge drift and route to data-ops.
- If single probe failure isolated to particular phrasing, add paraphrase probes to the bundle and re-evaluate under same snapshot.
- If regression is correlated with quantized rollout, use eval-runner --quant-compare to run both float and quantized variants anchored to the same snapshot for direct comparison.

Appendix B — Example policy table (default):
| domain_tag | snapshot_cadence | retention_days | canary_window | triage_owner |
| news | daily | 30 | 48h | data-ops |
| apis | weekly | 90 | 72h | product |
| knowledge-base | monthly | 365 | 7d | applied-ml |
